newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein says Netanyahu destroying peace.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein says Netanyahu destroying peace.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan has launched a bitter attack on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, accusing him of turning Middle East peace into a "distant elusive mirage".

In a letter sent to the Israeli leader, King Hussein said he had come to the conclusion Netanyahu was not a serious peace partner and accused of him of deception over his plans for Jewish settlements in the West Bank.
"My distress is genuine and deep over the accumulating tragic actions which you have initiated," King Hussein told Netanyahu in the letter, dated March 9 and made available to Reuters on Tuesday.
In his unprecedented outburst of frustration King Hussein, Israel's closest Arab ally since he signed a 1994 peace treaty with the Jewish state, scolded Netanyahu for spurning his "friendly" advice.

"You cannot send me assurances that you would not sanction any further construction of settlements...and then renege on your commitments," the king said. "I frankly cannot accept your repeated excuse of having to act the way you do under great duress and pressure."
Netanyahu's decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews around Arab East Jerusalem, announced just days after talks with King Hussein in Amman last month, prompted sharp criticism from Jordan.

The king also attacked Netanyahu's decision to limit a scheduled withdrawal from the West Bank to just nine percent of the land -- about a third of the area Palestinians had called for -- as "a deliberate humiliation of your so-called Palestinian partners".
"I could remain aloof if the very lives of all Arabs and Israelis and their future were not fast sliding towards an abyss of bloodshed, brought about by fear and despair," the king said.

"The saddest reality that has been dawning on me is that I do not find you by my side in working to fulfill God's will for the final reconciliation of the descendents of the children of Abraham," he added.
He said Netanyahu's actions made peace in the Middle East "appear more and more like a distant elusive mirage."
"How can I work with you as a partner and true friend in this confused and confusing atmosphere when I sense an intent to destroy all I worked to build between our peoples and state," the king said.
He said Netanyahu had even refused a personal request for the king, a keen aviator, to fly Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat back to Gaza after a visit to Amman.

"Suppose I had taken off nonetheless for Gaza, in the full right of a friend, then would you have ordered my fellow pilots in the Israeli Air Force...to prevent me forcibly from landing, or worse?" he asked.
"Stubborness over real issues is one thing, but for its own sake, I wonder," he said. "In any event, I have discovered that you have your own mindset and appear in no need for advice from a friend."

Netanyahu, asked about the king's letter during a visit to Moscow on Tuesday, was quoted as saying the king's remarks were not balanced, but King Hussein said he had a duty both to Arabs and Israelis to speak out.
